If you feel like you live in a movie and you have the ability to be 100% he is guilty, what then? Do you know that's a deterrent? Or do you assume because it feels correct? Maybe funding for mental health counseling and support for offenders *before* they abuse would stop 10x the abuse and the hurt, is it better our system waits until they harm someone before we do anything? And then you think the solution is to put them up against the wall? JusticePorn is about the smug satisfaction of seeing someone get their come-uppance, but real justice is about more than that. You can *never* be 100% sure. Not ever. Evidence isn't perfect. People lie and lie and lie and sincerely believe things that never happened because their memory filled it in. And it takes just one person you kill who isn't unambiguously, impeachably guilty, or is even baldly innocent, and then what? You're just a murdering thug spilling innocent blood on your vigilante hands. Should we up and shoot you next? As we aren't children, are we certain you'll do it again? Real justice is about due process. Real justice is about mercy. And it's about making compromises in a real world where we can never been 100% certain of what happened or did not happen, and it's about setting aside our feelings of being a vigilante and working on healing, and working on preventing, and working on recidivism and making sure we aren't making more criminals and people who do wrong when we try to stop it. Pardon me for my bluntness, but real heroes know their limitations, and know the world is not black and white, it is some very dark and very light greys, and those who say otherwise are often selling you a worldview and a bill of goods.

People who have a "fixed" mindset believe you're born with a certain capacity, or level of talent, or intelligence, or artistic skill, or genius, it cannot be changed, it is set. Versus the Growth mindset, which is the belief that one can work hard, be challenged and improve oneself through doing difficult things, making mistakes, and learning from the process. Children taught and immersed in the growth mindset do better in schooling, even controlling for many other factors: they believe they can get better, and they do. They have hope and positive expectations for the future, they don't believe they have to be perfect to be great. "I have free will" or "I'm in control of my own choices" is an extremely growth mindset oriented idea. Kids who believe their academic abilities are fixed, or are taught they have what they have to start are more willing to lie to make themselves look better, but less willing or able to work hard to achieve well in difficult material: they might fail, and then they would see themselves as a failure, and not escape the judgement of others and themselves. They are zealously guarding of their ego, because it is in danger from the world: being less than perfect means other people are better than you, and you're worse than them. You've got to look out for you if you believe that.
